gloss_hint: This means bracing for danger that has not yet arrived, scanning rooms for threats, and hedging every plan with what might go wrong, so that caution shapes what one says and does.
This means getting worked up quickly over small irritations and pressures, pacing or fidgeting, speaking faster and more sharply, and struggling to sit still until things settle.
This means choosing to spend most free hours without company, turning down invitations for quiet time alone, and speaking of solitude as the place where one thinks and recovers.
This means neglecting one's dress and grooming, letting clothes stay rumpled and dirty, hair go unbrushed, and treating tidiness as a bother not worth the effort.
This means losing the thread of conversations, forgetting appointments and names, and answering questions with muddled, half-finished thoughts because attention keeps drifting elsewhere.
This means dressing in heavy, glittering jewelry as a matter of course, drawing attention to one's rings and necklaces, and taking pride in an ornate, showy appearance.
This means keeping feelings at a distance, often seeming flat or absent when news lands, and going on with routines without much felt response.
This means losing interest quickly in whatever is happening, fidgeting through slow stretches, and complaining or changing the subject when a task drags on.
This means keeping one's body, clothes and surroundings spotless as a matter of routine, washing often, and feeling uneasy around dirt or grime.
This means fretting over possible problems before they happen, checking on things repeatedly, and voicing worries that others find out of proportion.
This means owning mistakes readily, apologizing at once, and carrying guilt for a long time after hurting someone, wanting to make amends.
This means snapping at small irritations, speaking curtly to people who interrupt, and showing displeasure in tone and expression long before anyone has done much wrong.
This means lighting up at small pleasures, such as a good meal, a kind remark or a bright morning, and saying so with warm, unguarded enthusiasm.
This means sinking easily into low spirits, seeing little point in plans, and speaking of the day's prospects in flat, heavy terms.
This means wanting things intensely and persistently, measuring one's contentment by what one still lacks, and letting envy of others' possessions color one's conversation.
This means talking as though one's future is already written, expecting doors to open and greatness to arrive, and brushing aside ordinary limits.
This means holding one's beliefs and commitments loosely, backing away from stated positions, and offering qualified, watered-down enthusiasm for whatever is asked of one.
This means recoiling readily from crude food, messes or bodily matters, and voicing one's revulsion bluntly while steering away from anything unpleasant.
This means finding fault with one's job, home and prospects, measuring every situation against something better, and voicing discontent to anyone who will listen.
This means letting attention slide off the task at hand toward whatever passes by, abandoning plans mid-sentence, and rarely finishing what one began.
This means picking arguments, taking sides in every dispute among colleagues or family, and carrying grudges forward into the next quarrel.
This means moving slowly through the day with little drive, answering in flat, low-energy tones, and letting tasks sit unfinished for want of the will to start them.
This means taking fire quickly at new ideas and projects, talking about them with bright energy, and pursuing them with an eagerness that others find infectious.
This means snapping at small delays and mistakes, sighing audibly at repeated requests, and running short of patience with people who keep asking the same things.
This means refusing food by deliberate choice on set days, speaking calmly about one's restraint, and turning down meals and treats that others take for granted.
This means letting one's body and clothes go unwashed for days, wearing the same grimy garments, and shrugging off remarks about the smell or the mess.
This means holding one's shoulders and jaw tight through the day, moving stiffly and quickly, and answering in clipped words as if braced for something.
This means fretting over small discomforts, whining about delays and minor slights, and voicing a steady stream of complaints that others find tiring.
This means going about with unwashed hair, rumpled and grimy clothes, and nails left dirty, showing little concern for how one looks to others.
This means drinking or using drugs to excess most days, chasing the lift they bring, and letting that habit steer one's money, time and company.
This means greeting new projects and ideas with eager energy, launching into them with fervor, and talking about them in glowing terms until the enthusiasm spreads to others around.
This means chafing against authority and rules, siding readily with those who defy the government, and speaking of rising up against unjust power with a fierce, restless anger.
This means dwelling on losses and disappointments, bemoaning what has gone wrong in a plaintive voice, and returning again and again to what was lost as if the grief were never quite finished.
This means finding humor in almost everything, breaking into laughter at small jokes and mishaps, and filling conversations with teasing remarks and easy giggles.
This means sliding into sermonizing whenever a topic arises, instructing friends on how they ought to live or think, and answering objections with a patient, superior tone of correction.
This means slipping easily into dejection, speaking of little that pleases, dragging through ordinary tasks, and answering friends with flat, weary replies.
This means sinking into gloomy listlessness over small disappointments, sulking when crossed, and answering questions with sighs and sullen short replies.
This means going flat and far away inside, meeting loss, joy and ordinary news with the same blank, and having to be prompted to say what one feels.
This means keeping phone and laptop switched off for long stretches, answering messages late or not at all, and feeling relieved rather than cut off when unreachable.
This means dwelling on a past wrong, apologizing repeatedly, and bringing up one's regret unprompted, often making amends and checking whether the hurt person has forgiven.
This means running out of energy well before others do, flagging after modest effort, and speaking of oneself as spent while everyone else is still going.
This means spending long, unhurried time on hair, clothes and makeup, checking one's reflection often, and remarking on how one looks as if appearance were a daily project.
This means wearing out quickly under pressure, letting fatigue and setbacks drain one's spirits, and sounding tired and flat when describing even ordinary demands.
This means losing composure at the slightest provocation, fumbling words, snapping at others, and reacting to small upsets with visible agitation before slowly regaining control.
This means bouncing back quickly after disappointment, reviving hope and enthusiasm for projects that had seemed finished, and talking about new beginnings with real energy.
This means rushing through tasks and conversations as a habit, speaking quickly, checking the clock often, and feeling impatient whenever one has to wait or slow down.
This means finding contentment easily in one's circumstances and possessions, taking little notice of what is missing, and speaking of what one has with quiet gratitude.
This means greeting other people's earnest plans and claims with a sneer and a mocking remark, treating enthusiasm as naive, and making scornful jokes at others' expense.
This means answering questions and requests with curt, irritable remarks, bristling at small delays or criticism, and letting irritation show in one's tone and manner.
This means abstaining from alcohol as a settled rule, turning down drinks at gatherings without apology, and keeping a clear head through evenings others spend drinking.
This means carrying a settled melancholy, dwelling on losses and disappointments, and speaking of hard things in a low, grieved voice as if sadness were the natural tone of life.
This means being knocked silent by news or events that others take in stride, standing motionless for a moment, and then struggling to find words for what just happened.
This means pausing before answering, turning questions over at length, and voicing conclusions only after weighing alternatives, so that others often wait for the thought to finish.
This means breaking into nervous giggles at tense moments, in serious meetings and at awkward silences, and covering one's own discomfort with laughter that others find hard to take seriously.
This means moving slowly through the day, answering questions after long pauses, and lacking the drive to start tasks, so that others must prod and wait for any response.
This means going days without washing, wearing the same unwashed clothes, and shrugging off the grime and odor that others notice around one.
This means feeling a low, persistent unease at ordinary events, scanning for what might go wrong, and voicing worries and second-guessing before others have raised any concern.
This means meeting good news and pleasant occasions with a flat response, finding little to enjoy, and speaking of life in a downcast, humorless tone.
This means losing composure at small surprises, stammering over simple questions, and fumbling tasks under mild pressure, so that one's speech comes out hurried and uncertain.
This means leaving oneself open to exploitation and attack, trusting people too readily, neglecting to guard one's money, reputation or feelings, and being hurt when others take advantage.
This means keeping a sober, grave face in company, speaking in a flat, serious tone, and treating jokes and small talk with reserved seriousness, so others take one for severe.
This means meeting setbacks and everyday demands with an even temper, letting small annoyances pass without comment, and speaking in a relaxed, unhurried way that reassures those around.
This means repeatedly letting others take one's time, money or favors without objection, saying yes to every request, and then feeling resentful and taken for granted when the cost is noticed.
This means drifting into blank, empty-headed stretches in conversation, with a fixed, far-off look, losing the thread of what is being said and needing a prompt to come back.
This means being caught by small wonders, such as a sunrise, a clever machine or a stranger's skill, stopping to stare, exclaiming in delight and wanting others to share the moment.
This means fretting over possible problems, rehearsing what could go wrong, and asking again and again for reassurance, so that small uncertainties keep one on edge.
